items.passage: Saving a part of income is one of the simplest habits that protects a family in difficult times. Even a small amount set aside every month can grow into a useful fund for medical needs, education or a sudden loss of income. The habit matters more than the amount, because regular saving builds discipline and reduces the need to borrow at high cost. Many households, however, spend first and save only what is left, which is often nothing. A better method is to save first, as soon as income arrives, and then plan spending around what remains. Banks, post offices and simple digital tools now make it easy to move a fixed sum into savings automatically. With this small change, families can face emergencies with less fear and plan for the future with more confidence.
items.question: What is the main benefit of regular saving, as per the passage?
options: It protects a family in difficult times
items.explanation: The passage states this directly or clearly implies it. The other options are not stated in the passage or contradict it.

items.question: Why does the author say the habit matters more than the amount?
options: Regular saving builds discipline and reduces costly borrowing
Saving is only for the rich
items.explanation: The passage states this directly or clearly implies it. The other options are not stated in the passage or contradict it.

options: Spend first and save the rest
Save first when income arrives, then plan spending
items.explanation: The passage states this directly or clearly implies it. The other options are not stated in the passage or contradict it.

items.explanation: The passage states this directly or clearly implies it. The other options are not stated in the passage or contradict it.

options: A small regular saving habit gives families security

items.explanation: The passage states this directly or clearly implies it. The other options are not stated in the passage or contradict it. The main-idea question needs the whole passage, not one line, so it is the hardest item in the set.

items.passage: Good public transport is the backbone of a liveable city. Buses and metro trains carry lakhs of people every day at a cost far lower than private cars, and they use far less road space per person. When buses are frequent, clean and on time, more people choose them, which reduces traffic jams and air pollution. Yet many cities still treat public transport as a last resort. Buses are crowded, routes are confusing and last-mile links to homes are weak. The solution is not only to buy more buses but to plan routes around where people live and work, to keep fares affordable and to give buses priority on busy roads. A city that invests in public transport invests in the time and health of its people.
items.question: Why is public transport called the backbone of a liveable city?
options: It replaces all cars at once
It carries lakhs daily at low cost and uses less road space
items.explanation: The passage states this directly or clearly implies it. The other options are not stated in the passage or contradict it.

items.explanation: The passage states this directly or clearly implies it. The other options are not stated in the passage or contradict it.

options: Plan routes around homes and work, keep fares affordable, give buses priority
items.explanation: The passage states this directly or clearly implies it. The other options are not stated in the passage or contradict it.

items.explanation: The passage states this directly or clearly implies it. The other options are not stated in the passage or contradict it. The main-idea question needs the whole passage, not one line, so it is the hardest item in the set.

items.question: Arrange the following sentences in a logical order: A. A small shop in the market began selling homemade pickles. B. The owner then hired two helpers and rented a bigger room. C. Soon the shop was taking orders from other towns as well. D. Word spread quickly because the pickles tasted fresh and different.
items.explanation: The correct order is ADCB. The sentence 'A small shop in the market began selling homemade pickles.' opens the paragraph by introducing the situation, and each following sentence continues it in sequence. The other orders break the flow, for example by placing the outcome before the event that caused it.

items.question: Arrange the following sentences in a logical order: A. The school library had very few books for young readers. B. Children began borrowing books every week and reading at home. C. The teachers collected donations and bought two hundred new books. D. Reading scores in the school improved within a year.
items.explanation: The correct order is ACBD. The sentence 'The school library had very few books for young readers.' opens the paragraph by introducing the situation, and each following sentence continues it in sequence. The other orders break the flow, for example by placing the outcome before the event that caused it.

items.question: Arrange the following sentences in a logical order: A. Online classes became common during the pandemic years. B. Results improved once the classes became shorter and more interactive. C. Teachers began using short videos and quick quizzes to hold attention. D. Many students found it hard to focus on a small screen all day.
items.explanation: The correct order is ADCB. The sentence 'Online classes became common during the pandemic years.' opens the paragraph by introducing the situation, and each following sentence continues it in sequence. The other orders break the flow, for example by placing the outcome before the event that caused it.

items.question: What is 15% of 400?
items.explanation: 15% of 400 is 400 x 15/100 = 60. The other options come from using a wrong percentage or a wrong base, which does not match the calculation.

items.question: A number is increased by 25% and becomes 625. What was the original number?
items.explanation: Let the original number be x. Then x x (100 + 25)/100 = 625, so x = 625 x 100/125 = 500. The other options divide by the wrong factor or add the percentage directly.

items.question: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 600 and sells it at a profit of 25%. What is the selling price?
items.explanation: Profit is 25% of Rs 600, which is Rs 150. Selling price is cost plus profit, Rs 600 + Rs 150 = Rs 750. The distractors ignore the profit or use the wrong percentage.

items.question: An article with cost price Rs 600 is marked at Rs 900 and sold at a discount of 20%. What is the profit percentage?
items.explanation: Discount is 20% of Rs 900, so the selling price is Rs 720. Profit is Rs 720 - Rs 600 = Rs 120, which is 20% of the cost price. The distractors use the marked price as the selling price or compute profit on the marked price.

items.question: Find the simple interest on Rs 5000 at 8% per annum for 3 years.
items.explanation: Simple interest is P x R x T / 100 = 5000 x 8 x 3 / 100 = Rs 1200. The distractors use a wrong time, a wrong rate, or forget to divide by 100.

items.question: What is the compound interest on Rs 20000 at 10% per annum for 2 years?
items.explanation: Amount after 2 years is 20000 x (1 + 10/100) squared = Rs 24200. Compound interest is amount minus principal, Rs 24200 - Rs 20000 = Rs 4200. Simple interest for 2 years would be lower, so options near the simple-interest amount are wrong.

items.question: Divide Rs 110 in the ratio 4:7. What is the first share?
items.explanation: Total parts are 4 + 7 = 11. Each part is Rs 110/11 = Rs 10. The first share is 4 parts, Rs 40. The other options give the second share or a wrong part value.

items.question: The average marks of 4 students are 50. Three of them scored 25, 45 and 65. What did the fourth student score?
items.explanation: Total marks of 4 students are 4 x 50 = 200. The three known scores add to 135, so the fourth score is 200 - 135 = 65. The distractors use the average itself or a wrong total.

items.question: A and B together can do a work in 10 days. A alone can do it in 30 days. In how many days can B alone do it?
items.explanation: Together they do 1/10 of the work per day and A does 1/30 per day. So B does 1/10 - 1/30 = 20/300 per day, which means B alone takes 15 days. Adding the days or averaging them gives the wrong options.

items.question: A car travels at 40 km/h for 3 hours. How far does it travel?
items.explanation: Distance is speed x time = 40 x 3 = 120 km. The distractors divide speed by time or add the two numbers, which does not give distance.

items.question: A train running at 54 km/h crosses a pole in 10 seconds. What is the length of the train?
items.explanation: Speed in m/s is 54 x 5/18 = 15 m/s. Length is speed x time = 15 x 10 = 150 metres. The distractors use km/h directly without converting to m/s.

items.question: In what ratio must milk costing Rs 40 per litre be mixed with water costing Rs 0 per litre to get a mixture worth Rs 30 per litre?
items.explanation: By alligation, the ratio of milk to water is (mixture price - water price) : (milk price - mixture price) = 30 : 10, which simplifies to 3:1. The reversed ratio is the most common mistake, and the other options do not satisfy the alligation rule.

items.question: The marked price of a shirt is Rs 500. It is sold at a discount of 25%. What is the selling price?
items.explanation: Discount is 25% of Rs 500, Rs 125. Selling price is Rs 500 - Rs 125 = Rs 375. The discount amount itself is a distractor.

items.question: What is the HCF of 15 and 20?
items.explanation: Factors of 15 include 5 and factors of 20 also include 5, and no larger number divides both. So the HCF is 5. The LCM 60 is a distractor.

items.question: What is the LCM of 15 and 20?
items.explanation: The smallest number divisible by both 15 and 20 is 60. The HCF 5 and the product are distractors.

items.question: What is the smallest number which when divided by 4 and 6 leaves a remainder of 3 in each case?
items.explanation: The number must be 3 more than a common multiple of 4 and 6. The LCM of 4 and 6 is 12, so the smallest such number is 12 + 3 = 15. The distractors use the LCM alone or add the wrong remainder.

items.question: What is the unit digit of 8 raised to the power 21?
items.explanation: The unit digits of powers of 8 repeat in a cycle of 4. Using that cycle, 8 to the power 21 ends in 8. The other digits come from using the wrong position in the cycle.

items.question: What is the square of 13?
items.explanation: The square of 13 is 13 x 13 = 169. The other options are the number doubled or a nearby square, which do not match.

items.question: If 4x + 3 = 19, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Subtract 3 from both sides to get 4x = 16, then divide by 4 to get x = 4. The other options add the constant instead of subtracting it or divide by the wrong number.

items.question: If 2x + 9 = 3x + 5, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Bring the x terms together: 2x - 3x = 5 - 9, so -1x = -4, which gives x = 4. The other options move the terms to the wrong side or miss a sign.

items.question: What is the sum of the roots of x squared - 7x + 10 = 0?
items.explanation: The quadratic factors as (x - 2)(x - 5), so the roots are 2 and 5. Their sum is 7. The other options use the coefficients directly without factoring, which gives the wrong value.

items.question: The sum of two numbers is 40 and their difference is 8. What is the larger number?
items.explanation: Let the numbers be x and y. Adding the equations x + y = 40 and x - y = 8 gives 2x = 48, so x = 24. The smaller number 16 is a distractor.

items.question: The ratio of the ages of A and B is 5:3. After 6 years, the ratio becomes 7:5. What is the present age of A?
items.explanation: Let the ages be 5k and 3k. After 6 years, (5k + 6)/(3k + 6) = 7/5. Solving gives k = 3, so A is 5 x 3 = 15 years old. The other options use the ratio directly without solving for k.

items.question: What is the area of a rectangle 15 m long and 10 m wide?
items.explanation: Area is length x breadth = 15 x 10 = 150 sq m. The perimeter is a different value and is a distractor.

items.question: What is the area of a circle with radius 14 cm? (Use pi = 22/7)
items.explanation: Area is pi x r squared = 22/7 x 14 x 14 = 616 sq cm. Using the diameter instead of the radius, or forgetting to square the radius, gives the wrong options.

items.question: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 12 m long and 9 m wide?
items.explanation: Perimeter is 2 x (length + breadth) = 2 x (12 + 9) = 42 m. The area is a different value and is a distractor.

items.question: What is the volume of a cuboid 6 cm long, 5 cm wide and 4 cm high?
items.explanation: Volume is length x breadth x height = 6 x 5 x 4 = 120 cubic cm. The surface area is a different value and is a distractor.

items.question: In how many ways can 2 letters be chosen and arranged from 6 different letters without repetition?
items.explanation: The first place can be filled in 6 ways, the next in 5 ways, and so on for 2 places, giving 30 arrangements in total. The distractors count combinations without order, which is smaller.

items.question: A bag has 3 red balls and 7 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red?
items.explanation: There are 10 balls in total and 3 of them are red, so the probability is 3/10 = 3/10. The other fractions use the blue count or the wrong total.

items.question: In a class of 80 students, 40 play cricket, 30 play football and 15 play both. How many play neither game?
items.explanation: Students playing at least one game are 40 + 30 - 15 = 55, because the 15 who play both were counted twice. Those playing neither are 80 - 55 = 25. The distractors forget to subtract the overlap.

items.question: What is the total production of Rice over the four years (in tonnes)?

diagram.caption: Production (in tonnes) of four crops, 2021 to 2024

items.explanation: Add Rice production: 82 + 85 + 89 + 82 = 338 tonnes. The other options add the wrong column or miss a year.

items.question: In which year was the production of Wheat the highest?
items.explanation: Wheat production is [83, 62, 64, 41] for 2021 to 2024, highest 83 in 2021. The other years have lower values, so they are not the peak year.

items.question: What is the total production of all crops in 2024 (in tonnes)?
items.explanation: Add the 2024 row: 82 + 41 + 79 + 50 = 252 tonnes. Adding a different year gives a wrong total.

items.question: By how much did Maize production increase from 2021 to 2024 (in tonnes)?
items.explanation: Maize rose from 62 to 79, an increase of 17 tonnes. The distractors use other crops or subtract the wrong way.

items.question: What is the average yearly production of Pulses (in tonnes)?
items.explanation: Total of Pulses is 231 over 4 years, average 231/4 = 57 tonnes (rounded down to the nearest whole number in the table). The total itself is a distractor.

items.question: What is the number of employees in the largest department?

diagram.caption: Number of employees in five departments

items.explanation: The bars are {'Sales': 91, 'Support': 156, 'R&D': 118, 'Admin': 155, 'Logistics': 110}. The largest value is 156. Smaller bars are the distractors.

items.question: What is the total number of employees in all five departments?
items.explanation: Add all bars: 91 + 156 + 118 + 155 + 110 = 630. Missing one department gives a lower total.

items.question: What is the difference between the largest and the smallest number of employees across the five departments?
items.explanation: Largest is 156 and smallest is 91, difference 65. Adding them instead gives a wrong answer.

items.question: What is the average number of employees per department?
items.explanation: Total 630 over 5 departments gives an average of 126. The total itself is a distractor, and using only the largest department would also give a wrong answer.

items.question: How many more employees are in Support than in Sales?
items.explanation: Support has 156 and Sales has 91, difference 65. The reverse subtraction would be negative, so the positive difference is correct.

items.question: A family spends Rs 50000 a month. If EMI is 35% of spending in the pie chart (EMI, Groceries, Fuel, Entertainment, Savings), how much is spent on EMI?
items.explanation: EMI is 35% of Rs 50000, which is Rs 17500. Using another slice percentage gives a wrong amount.

items.question: What is the largest share of spending in the pie chart (EMI, Groceries, Fuel, Entertainment, Savings)?
items.explanation: The shares are [35, 8, 25, 20, 12] percent. The largest is 35%. Smaller slices are distractors.

items.question: What is the combined share of Groceries and Fuel (in percent)?
items.explanation: Groceries is 8% and Fuel is 25%, together 33%. Adding other slices gives a wrong total.

items.question: If total spending is Rs 50,000, how much is spent on Savings in the pie chart (EMI, Groceries, Fuel, Entertainment, Savings)?
items.explanation: Savings is 12% of Rs 50,000, which is Rs 6000. The distractors use other slice percentages, which give different amounts.

items.question: What is the difference between the largest and smallest shares in the spending pie chart (EMI, Groceries, Fuel, Entertainment, Savings)?
items.explanation: Largest share is 35% and smallest is 8%, difference 27 points. Adding them instead of subtracting gives a wrong answer.

items.question: What is the value of x? I. x + 3 = 9. II. x - 2 = 4.
items.explanation: Statement I alone gives x = 9 - 3 = 6, and statement II alone gives x = 4 + 2 = 6. Either statement alone is enough to find the value. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: Is x greater than y? I. x = 20. II. y = 16.
items.explanation: Neither statement alone compares x and y, but together x = 20 and y = 16, so x is greater than y. Both statements together are needed. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: What is the profit on the article? I. Cost price is Rs 600. II. Selling price is Rs 700.
items.explanation: Cost price alone or selling price alone cannot give profit. Together, profit is Rs 700 - Rs 600 = Rs 100. Both statements together are needed. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: What is the perimeter of the rectangle? I. Length is 18 m. II. Breadth is 6 m.
items.explanation: Length alone or breadth alone cannot give perimeter. Together, perimeter is 2 x (18 + 6) = 48 m. Both statements together are needed. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: Is the number divisible by 3? I. The sum of its digits is 12. II. The number is 36.
items.explanation: Statement I alone is enough, because a number whose digit sum is 12 is divisible by 3. Statement II alone is also enough, because 36 is divisible by 3. Either statement alone suffices. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: What is the area of the rectangle? I. Length is 12 m. II. Breadth is 8 m.
items.explanation: Length alone or breadth alone cannot give area. Together, area is 12 x 8 = 96 sq m. Both statements together are needed. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: How many students are in the class? I. There are 30 boys. II. Girls are half the number of boys.
items.explanation: Statement I gives boys only. Statement II relates girls to boys but needs the boy count. Together: 30 boys and 15 girls, total 45. Both together are needed. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: Is n divisible by 6? I. n is divisible by 2. II. n is divisible by 3.
items.explanation: Divisibility by 2 alone or by 3 alone does not imply divisibility by 6. Together, a number divisible by both 2 and 3 is divisible by 6. Both together are needed. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: How many mangoes are there in the basket? I. There are 30 fruits in total. II. Mangoes and oranges are in the ratio 1:2.
items.explanation: Statement I gives only the total and statement II only the ratio. Together, mangoes are 1/3 of 30, which is 10. Both together are needed. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: What is the HCF of the two numbers? I. The numbers are 15 and 20. II. Their product is 300.
items.explanation: Statement I alone gives the numbers, so their HCF is 5. Statement II alone gives only the product, which does not fix the HCF. So statement I alone suffices. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: What is the value of x? I. x + y = 26. II. x - y = 10.
items.explanation: Neither statement alone gives x, because each has two unknowns. Together, adding them gives 2x = 36, so x = 18. Both statements together are needed. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: What is the value of y? I. y + 3 = 8. II. 2y = 10.
items.explanation: Statement I alone gives y = 8 - 3 = 5, and statement II alone gives y = 10/2 = 5. Either statement alone is enough to find the value. The other options claim a different statement is enough, which does not follow from the given facts.

items.question: In a survey, 180 people prefer product X and 50 prefer product Y. How many people were surveyed in total (assuming each chose one)?
items.explanation: Total is 180 + 50 = 230, since each person chose one product. The distractors subtract or use only one group.

items.question: In a survey, 80 people like tea, 70 like coffee and 10 like neither. How many people were surveyed in total?
items.explanation: Add all three groups: 80 + 70 + 10 = 160. The distractors leave out the group that likes neither.

items.question: In a survey, 70 people like tea, 50 like coffee and 25 like both. How many people like only tea?
items.explanation: Those who like only tea are the tea lovers minus those who like both: 70 - 25 = 45. The total tea lovers 70 is a distractor, because it includes the overlap.

items.question: Rohan is the father of Ravi. Ravi is the sister of Priya. How is Rohan related to Priya?
items.explanation: Rohan is the father of Ravi, and Ravi and Priya are siblings, so Rohan is also the father of Priya. Uncle and grandfather do not fit.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Blood Relations

items.question: Amit is the brother of Divya. Divya is the mother of Kavya. How is Amit related to Kavya?
items.explanation: Amit is the brother of Kavya's mother, so he is Kavya's uncle. Father and brother do not fit, because Amit is one generation above Kavya, not the father or a sibling.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Blood Relations

items.question: Sita is Vikram's wife. Vikram is Rohan's father. How is Sita related to Rohan?
items.explanation: Vikram is Rohan's father and Sita is Vikram's wife, so Sita is Rohan's mother. Aunt and sister do not fit, because neither is the wife of Rohan's father.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Blood Relations

items.question: Divya is the son of Kavya. Kavya is the brother of Sita. Sita is the mother of Vikram. How is Divya related to Vikram?
items.explanation: Divya's parent Kavya and Vikram's parent Sita are siblings, so Divya and Vikram are cousins. Brother and uncle do not fit, because they belong to a different generation or relation.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Blood Relations

items.question: If FOX is coded as GPY, how is SUN coded?
items.explanation: Each letter moves one step forward: FOX becomes GPY. Applying the same shift to SUN gives TVO. The other options use a different shift or no shift at all.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Coding Decoding

items.question: If CUP is coded as BTO, how is FOX coded?
items.explanation: Each letter moves one step back: CUP becomes BTO. Applying the same shift to FOX gives ENW. The other options move letters forward or use a different shift.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Coding Decoding

items.question: If FAN is coded as OBG, how is PEN coded?
items.explanation: The word is first reversed and then each letter moves one step forward: FAN reversed is NAF, which becomes OBG. Applying the same rule to PEN gives OFQ. The other options skip the reversal or use a different shift.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Coding Decoding

items.question: If FIRE is coded as 69185, how is BIRD coded?
items.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its position in the alphabet: FIRE becomes 69185. Applying the same rule to BIRD gives 29184. The other options shift the positions or leave the word unchanged.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Coding Decoding

items.question: What is the next number in the series: 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, ?
items.explanation: Each term increases by 4, so the next term is 18 + 4 = 22. The other options do not follow the pattern.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Number Series

items.question: What is the next number in the series: 2, 6, 18, 54, 162, ?
items.explanation: Each term is multiplied by 3, so the next term is 162 x 3 = 486. The other options add instead of multiplying.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Number Series

items.question: What is the next number in the series: 1, 4, 5, 9, 14, ?
items.explanation: Each term is the sum of the previous two, so the next term is 14 + 9 = 23. The other options do not follow the pattern.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Number Series

items.question: What is the next letter in the series: A, D, G, J, ?
items.explanation: Letters increase by 3 each time, so the next letter after J is M. The other letters do not follow the +3 step.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Letter Series

items.question: What is the next letter in the series: A, B, E, J, Q, ?
items.explanation: Gaps grow each step (+1, +3, +5, +7), so the next gap is +9 and Q + 9 = Z. The other letters use a fixed gap, which does not match the growing gaps in the series.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Letter Series

items.question: Statements: All dogs are pets. All pets are animals. Conclusion: All dogs are animals.
items.explanation: If all dogs are pets and all pets are animals, then all dogs must be animals. The chain of inclusion makes the conclusion follow.

items.question: Statements: Some pens are pencils. All pencils are stationery items. Conclusion: Some pens are stationery items.
items.explanation: Some pens are pencils, and every pencils is a stationery items, so those pens are stationery items. The conclusion follows.

items.question: Statements: No cars is a vehicles. Some vehicles are machines. Conclusion: Some machines are not cars.
items.explanation: The machines that are vehicles cannot be cars, since no vehicles is a cars. So some machines are not cars, and the conclusion follows.

items.question: In a group of 80 people, 40 like tea, 30 like coffee and 15 like both. How many like only tea?
items.explanation: Those who like only tea are the tea lovers minus those who like both: 40 - 15 = 25. The total tea lovers 40 is a distractor, because it includes the overlap.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Venn Diagrams

items.question: In a group of 80 people, 40 like tea, 30 like coffee and 15 like both. How many like only coffee?
items.explanation: Those who like only coffee are the coffee lovers minus those who like both: 30 - 15 = 15. The total coffee lovers 30 is a distractor, because it includes the overlap.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Venn Diagrams

items.question: In a group of 80 people, 40 like tea, 30 like coffee and 15 like both. How many like neither?
items.explanation: People liking at least one drink are 40 + 30 - 15 = 55, because the 15 who like both were counted twice. Those liking neither are 80 - 55 = 25. The distractors forget to subtract the overlap.

items.question: Statement: People who read news daily score better on general knowledge tests. What is the most careful inference?
options: News reading is the only way to learn
People who do not read news know nothing
Reading news is linked to better scores, but other habits may also matter
items.explanation: The statement shows a link between news reading and test scores, not proof that news alone causes them. Other habits, such as schooling or reading books, may also matter. The other options overstate the link.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Critical Reasoning

items.question: Statement: Traffic fines were doubled and violations fell by 40 percent. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Fines are the only way to stop violations
Higher fines may have discouraged violations, though other measures could also have helped
All drivers now obey every rule
items.explanation: Violations fell after fines rose, which supports a deterrent effect, but the data alone do not prove fines were the only cause. The careful conclusion allows other factors. The other options claim more than the data show.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Critical Reasoning

items.question: Statement: A new road is built and travel time falls. What can be concluded?
options: The road may have shortened travel, though traffic levels also matter
Travel time will keep falling forever
New roads always cut travel time
items.explanation: Travel time fell after the road opened, which suggests the road helped, but traffic levels and other changes also affect travel time. The modest conclusion allows those factors. The other options claim too much.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Critical Reasoning

items.question: Statement: A bank cuts its home loan rate and home loan applications rise. Which strengthens the claim that the rate cut caused the rise?
options: The bank also opened new branches
The bank spent more on advertising
No other bank changed its rates and house prices stayed the same in that period
items.explanation: If nothing else changed, the rate cut is the most likely cause of the rise. That strengthens the claim. The other options add alternative causes, which would weaken it instead.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Critical Reasoning

items.question: Statement: Two towns have the same population, but Town A has twice as many parks as Town B. Town A also has fewer cases of lifestyle disease. What can be inferred?
options: Parks may encourage activity, but the data do not prove parks alone cause better health
Every town needs twice as many parks
Town B has no healthy people
items.explanation: The towns differ in parks and in disease, which suggests a link, but diet, income and jobs could also differ. The careful inference allows those factors. The other options claim a cure or a universal rule the data do not support.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Critical Reasoning

items.question: A person faces North, turns left then turns left then turns left. Which direction does the person face now?
items.explanation: Starting from North, each turn changes the direction. After turning left then turns left then turns left, the person faces East. The other options skip a turn or turn the wrong way.

items.question: A man walks 6 km south, then 8 km west. How far is he from the starting point?
items.explanation: The path forms a right triangle with sides 6 and 8, so the straight distance is the square root of 6 squared + 8 squared, which is 10 km. Adding the two legs gives 14 km, which is the path length, not the straight distance.
items.topic: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning - Direction Sense
